name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
hook: Four elections, the New Deal and "a date which will live in infamy" — FDR in seven facts.

facts.label: the New Deal
facts.statement: The New Deal was his economic recovery and social reform program; the "second New Deal" began with his January 4, 1935 message to Congress.

facts.label: Fireside Chats
facts.statement: He gave the first of his "Fireside Chats" on March 12, 1933, speaking from the White House diplomatic reception room.

facts.label: Good Neighbor Policy
facts.statement: His Good Neighbor Policy toward Latin America stressed nonintervention and improved U.S. relations there.

facts.label: "Infamy" speech
facts.statement: In his December 8, 1941 speech he called December 7 "a date which will live in infamy" and asked Congress for war.

facts.label: Casablanca Conference
facts.statement: At Casablanca in 1943 he and Churchill agreed to invade "the soft underbelly of the Axis."

facts.label: Yalta
facts.statement: In February 1945 he met Churchill and Stalin at Yalta in the Crimea; his daughter Anna went with him.

facts.label: Warm Springs
facts.statement: He died in office in April 1945; his will left $560,000 in insurance to the Warm Springs Foundation in Georgia.
